original_description: Drive the day-to-day stacked-branch authoring loop with the `git-stack` CLI: syncing against upstream, viewing the stack, navigating between commits/branches, editing earlier commits (amend/reword/fixup), running checks across the stack, and restacking branches onto new bases. Use this WHENEVER the user is working with stacked branches or stacked PRs, mentions `git-stack`/`git stack`/`git sync`/ `git next`/`git prev`/`git amend`/`git reword`, asks to "rebase my stack", "sync my branches", "edit an earlier commit", "fix up a parent commit", "navigate the stack", or "run tests across the stack" — even if they don't name git-stack explicitly but the repo clearly uses a stacked-diff workflow. For pushing branches as PRs use `git-stack-publish`; for undoing/repairing a broken stack use `git-stack-recover`.

final_description: Use when someone working with stacked branches, stacked commits, or stacked PRs wants to build or revise that stack — especially with the `git-stack` CLI, but trigger even if they only say "git stack" or describe the workflow. Fires for any of these intents: sync or rebase the whole stack onto an updated upstream/main at the start of the day; amend or fold staged changes into an earlier (or HEAD) commit and carry the descendants along; reword an earlier/parent commit's message and bring its children; fold a `fixup!` commit into its target further down the stack; jump to or edit the Nth commit down (e.g. fix a typo in the 2nd commit) without breaking the commits above it; or run a build/test command across every commit in the stack. In short: editing or restacking earlier commits while keeping children rebased. For pushing or opening stacked PRs use `git-stack-publish`; for conflicts, lost branches, or undoing a rewrite use `git-stack-recover`.

Trigger for: syncing/rebasing the whole stack onto updated upstream main; amending or folding staged changes into an earlier (non-HEAD) commit and carrying the descendants along; rewording an ancestor commit's message; folding a `fixup!` commit into its target lower in the stack; navigating to or editing the Nth commit down without breaking the commits above it; or running a build/test command against every commit in the stack. Assume these apply whenever the user describes editing earlier commits and keeping children rebased, even without naming `git-stack`. For pushing/opening PRs use `git-stack-publish`; for conflicts, lost branches, or undoing a rewrite use `git-stack-recover`.
